issues.body: require_one_side_bound remains a standalone helper whose documentation says callers should run it before wire::derive_grants. No changed production boundary invokes it, and the acceptance tests call the helper directly rather than submitting controller-authored rule text through the real admission path. Callers can therefore still pass unseedable .acr text directly to derive_grants despite the fail-closed guard language.
issues.fix_hint: Enforce require_one_side_bound at the shared boundary where controller-authored .acr text enters derive_grants/evaluation, propagate denial fail-closed, and add an integration test proving an unseeded rule is rejected through that real path while a seeded rule succeeds. Alternatively, consistently narrow the public claims to an optional static-analysis helper and explicitly leave operational enforcement unresolved.
issues.title: Fail-closed seeding guard remains unenforced on the real .acr path

issues.body: is_var still recognizes only terms beginning with '?', so term_bound treats a blank-node label such as '_:x' as a bound constant. Within an N3 rule formula that label is formula-scoped/existential, not an externally fixed endpoint, and cannot conservatively supply the constant-side lookup promised by this analysis. For example, `{ _:x p:linkedTo ?o } => { ?o p:ok p:v }` can still pass incorrectly.
issues.fix_hint: Treat blank-node labels as formula-scoped unbound terms for seeding analysis, or reject them as unsupported. Add a require_one_side_bound regression test proving a blank-node-labelled endpoint cannot seed an otherwise unbound atom.
issues.title: Blank-node labels are still incorrectly accepted as constant seeds

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant. Both prior major findings remain unchanged: require_one_side_bound is still only a public helper that documentation tells callers to invoke, while no production .acr admission boundary enforces it and the tests still call the helper directly. Blank-node labels remain classified as constants because is_var recognizes only '?' variables, so a formula-scoped existential endpoint can still incorrectly seed an atom. The new feature-matrix leg improves test execution coverage but does not resolve either correctness gap.
